title: Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana Blast India to Series Win Over Zimbabwe
excerpt: India chased 103 in 8.5 overs in Raipur as Shafali Verma hit 55 and Smriti Mandhana 47 not out, after the bowlers held Zimbabwe to 102 for 8 in the second T20I.
body:
• India beat Zimbabwe by nine wickets in the second T20I in Raipur on Sunday to take an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match series.
  • Shafali Verma smashed 55 off 25 balls and captain Smriti Mandhana finished unbeaten on 47 off 25, their 96-run opening stand ending the chase in 8.5 overs with 67 balls to spare.
  • India's bowlers restricted Zimbabwe to 102 for 8, with Niki Prasad taking 2 for 7 in two overs and five bowlers taking at least one wicket.
  • The win was India's 17th T20I victory of 2026, their most in a calendar year, and the biggest win by balls remaining when chasing more than 100 in women's T20Is.

India sealed the three-match T20I series against Zimbabwe with a nine-wicket win in the second match at the Shaheed Veer Narayan Singh International Stadium in Raipur on Sunday. Chasing 103, India reached 104 for 1 in 8.5 overs, finishing the contest with 67 balls to spare after their bowlers had limited Zimbabwe to 102 for 8 in 20 overs, according to ESPNcricinfo. The result gave Smriti Mandhana a series win at the start of her tenure as full-time captain, following India's four-wicket win in Friday's opener.

Bowlers squeeze Zimbabwe from the start

Zimbabwe chose to bat first but never built momentum on a slow, grippy surface. Mandhana had said at the toss that she wanted India to be more disciplined with the ball, and her attack delivered. Kranti Gaud and Nandani Sharma shared the new ball, and Zimbabwe crawled to 20 for 1 in the powerplay, playing 29 dot balls in the first six overs. Opener Kelis Ndhlovu was dismissed for an 11-ball duck by Nandani Sharma, and Beloved Biza fell to Deepti Sharma shortly after the powerplay. Zimbabwe faced 71 dot balls in the innings.

Chipo Mugeri-Tiripano and captain Josephine Nkomo provided the only sustained resistance. Mugeri-Tiripano top-scored with 34 off 32 balls, using reverse sweeps to collect boundaries, and added 45 runs with Nkomo for the fourth wicket. She survived two dropped catches before Niki Prasad broke the stand in the 15th over. Prasad dismissed Mugeri-Tiripano, caught behind by Richa Ghosh, and trapped Nyasha Gwanzura leg-before with her next ball, taking two wickets with her first two deliveries and finishing with 2 for 7. Nkomo remained unbeaten on 27 off 35 balls as Zimbabwe closed on 102 for 8. Gaud took 1 for 15, Deepti Sharma 1 for 13, and Shree Charani also took a wicket as five of Mandhana's seven bowlers struck.

Shafali and Mandhana finish the chase in fast-forward

India's reply was the opposite of Zimbabwe's innings. Shafali Verma attacked from the first over, hitting a four and a six off Nyasha Gwanzura, and Mandhana joined in with back-to-back boundaries as India raced to 40 without loss in four overs. In the fifth over, Mandhana hit Gwanzura for four consecutive fours in an over that cost 21 runs, and India ended the powerplay at 76 for 0.

Shafali reached her half-century off 24 balls with a six over deep mid-wicket and was dismissed by Beloved Biza on the next ball for 55 off 25, with six fours and four sixes. By then the 96-run opening stand, made in 47 balls, had left India needing seven runs. Mandhana, unbeaten on 47 off 25 with six fours and two sixes, finished the match with a six in the ninth over. Shafali was named Player of the Match.

"I thought that was a batting masterclass by the Indian team. We just stood there and had to watch and learn, and there's no better way to learn than actually experiencing the carnage that happened out there."

— Josephine Nkomo, Zimbabwe captain

Records for the opening pair

The partnership carried milestones beyond the series result. Shafali and Mandhana became the first pair to aggregate more than 1,000 runs together in a single calendar year in women's T20Is, and their stand was their ninth worth 50 or more in 2026. Shafali also became the first woman to pass 900 T20I runs in a calendar year, reaching 922 runs in 2026, ahead of South Africa captain Laura Wolvaardt on 824. For diaspora fans who follow the women's game closely, the numbers underline how central the opening pair has become to India's T20I side this year.

What is next

The third and final T20I is in Raipur on Tuesday, October 20, with India chasing a 3-0 clean sweep and Zimbabwe playing to avoid a whitewash. Nkomo said her side's priority was a better powerplay start with the bat after managing only 20 runs in the first six overs. With the series decided, India have a chance to test their bench strength, while Zimbabwe need a stronger total to put India's batting under any pressure.
